lines.japanese: それから当てもなく校内を散策して、集合時間の十分前に教室へ戻った。
lines.english: Afterward I wandered the school without destination and returned to the classroom ten minutes before we were due to meet.

lines.japanese: 集合時間、とは言っても高内さんは「１時“ぐらい”」と指定した。失礼かもしれないけど、たぶん少し遅れてくるだろう。
lines.english: Though ‘due to meet’ was perhaps too exact. Takauchi had specified ‘around one.’ It might be unkind to say so, but she would probably arrive a little late.

lines.japanese: 誰もいない机のあいだを歩いて、自分の席に腰を下ろした。
lines.english: I walked between the empty desks and sat down at my own.

lines.japanese: そうだ、誰もいないなら……僕は他にすることもないので、本当は校則で禁止されている携帯電話を片手で開いた。
lines.english: That was right—if no one was here… With nothing else to do, I flipped open the cell phone that school rules technically forbade.

lines.japanese: ぼんやり見下ろすと、ディスプレイの上の方にちょこんと新着メールのアイコンが灯っていた。誰からだろう、根拠のない期待に胸が躍る。受信トレイを慌てて開けた。
lines.english: I glanced absently down. At the top of the display, the tiny icon for a new message glowed. Who could it be? My heart leaped with groundless hope, and I hurriedly opened the inbox.

lines.japanese: 『♪女子大生ミ～コ☆　さぴちぃ夜☆彡は　Ｈな㊦半身がウズ×２しＣＨＡゥの～↑↑』
lines.english: ‘♪ College Cutie Mi~ko☆ On lonely nights☆彡 my naughty lower half gets all tingly-wingly~↑↑’

lines.japanese: 僕は小さな息をつき、手を机の上に下ろした。
lines.english: I breathed a small sigh and lowered my hand to the desk.

lines.japanese: 『未読メールを削除しますか？』
lines.english: ‘Delete unread message?’

lines.japanese: 『はい』
lines.english: ‘Yes.’

lines.japanese: さまざまな対策が練られて一時期に比べればだいぶ減りはしたけど、いまでもたまに未承諾広告は送りつけられる。
lines.english: Various countermeasures had made unsolicited advertisements far less common than they once were, but even now one occasionally forced its way through.

lines.japanese: みんな、そんなに出会いを求めているんだろうか。ミ～コ☆さんとやらには悪いけど、僕はいまのところぜんぜん寂しくなんかない。寂しいだなんて、いままで一度だって思ったことはない。
lines.english: Was everyone truly so desperate to meet someone? I felt sorry for Mi~ko☆ or whatever her name was, but at present I was not lonely in the least. Never once in my life had I thought myself lonely.

lines.japanese: ほんとうだよ。
lines.english: It was true.

lines.japanese: べったりと机に突っぷし、携帯電話のメモ帳を開く。
lines.english: I collapsed flat over the desk and opened the notepad on my phone.

lines.japanese: “２：学食のチキンソテー＆エビフライ定食を食べる”
lines.english: ‘2: Eat the sautéed chicken and fried shrimp meal in the cafeteria.’

lines.japanese: カーソルをそこへ運んで行頭の一文字を──
lines.english: I moved the cursor there and changed the first character—

lines.japanese: “済：学食のチキンソテー＆エビフライ定食を食べる”
lines.english: ‘DONE: Eat the sautéed chicken and fried shrimp meal in the cafeteria.’

lines.japanese: ──よし。あと四つ。
lines.english: —good. Four left.

lines.japanese: 胸の中でつぶやき、握りつぶすようにケータイを畳んだ。
lines.english: I whispered the words inside my chest and snapped the phone shut as though crushing it in my fist.

lines.japanese: 壁時計を見上げる。前後の扉を確認する。高内さんはまだ現れない。きっと食後の歓談が長引いているんだろう。
lines.english: I looked up at the wall clock, then checked both doors. Takauchi had yet to appear. Conversation after lunch must have run long.

lines.japanese: ふぅ……。
lines.english: Haaah…

lines.japanese: 手持ち無沙汰をしのぐため、一度は閉じた携帯電話をまた開いた。新しい着信メロディでも探しに行こう。
lines.english: To relieve the idleness, I reopened the phone I had just closed. Perhaps I would look for a new ringtone.

lines.japanese: いくつか音楽サイトをまわって、ひと昔前に流れた笑えるＣＭのインスト曲を見つけた。もしこれが森里君の前で流れたりすれば、ささやかな笑いが取れるかもしれない。
lines.english: After visiting several music sites, I found the instrumental from an amusing commercial that had aired years before. If it happened to play in front of Morisato, it might earn a modest laugh.

lines.japanese: だけどダウンロードする前にふと思った。そういえば、いまの着メロはなんだったっけ。もう何週間も電話がかかってきてないから忘れてしまった。
lines.english: Before downloading it, however, a thought came to me. What was my present ringtone, anyway? No one had called me in weeks, and I had forgotten.

lines.japanese: ケータイは僕にとって音声伝達手段ではなく、暇つぶしのインターネット閲覧用端末だ。これの番号を知っているのは、僕と家族と行きつけのお店ぐらい。
lines.english: To me, a cell phone was no instrument for transmitting voices. It was a handheld terminal for browsing the internet when I had time to kill. Only I, my family, and a few shops I frequented knew its number.

lines.japanese: 僕はネット閲覧用端末を閉じて、また教室の壁時計を見上げる。１時をちょっと過ぎていた。予想通り。
lines.english: I closed my internet terminal and looked up at the classroom clock again. A little after one. Just as expected.

lines.japanese: 視線が渡来さんの机に寄り道すると、潰えた約束に思わず溜息がこぼれた。本当ならいまごろ──
lines.english: My gaze strayed to Watarai’s desk, and the broken promise drew an involuntary sigh from me. By now, if things had gone as planned—

lines.japanese: ──考えたって詮もないことを忘れるため、みたび端末を開いた。
lines.english: —there was no use imagining it. To forget, I opened the terminal for the third time.

lines.japanese: 机の上に腕を伸ばし、その上に頬を載せる。そんなだらしのない姿勢で、僕は内蔵されている他愛もないミニゲームを始めた。
lines.english: I stretched an arm across the desk and rested my cheek upon it. Sprawled there so slovenly, I began one of the trivial games built into the phone.

lines.japanese: ケータイのぴこぴこ。
lines.english: Beep-boops on my phone.

lines.japanese: それから一時間が経った。
lines.english: An hour passed.

lines.japanese: 僕はまだ机の上でだらしのない姿勢を続けていた。
lines.english: I was still sprawled untidily over the desk.

lines.japanese: チープな電子音と硬いボタンの押下音とが、誰もいない教室にうるさいぐらい響いていた。
lines.english: The cheap electronic tones and hard clicks of the buttons rang almost deafeningly through the empty classroom.

lines.japanese: ぴこぴこ、かちかち、ぴこぴこ、かちかち……。
lines.english: Beep-boop, click-click, beep-boop, click-click…

lines.japanese: ケータイ標準装備のパズルゲームは、明らかにゲーム慣れしてないユーザーを意識した難易度設定。すでにコツを掴んでしまった僕には、手を離しでもしないかぎり終わりようのない有様だった。
lines.english: The puzzle game supplied with the phone had clearly been tuned for users unfamiliar with games. Now that I had grasped its trick, it seemed incapable of ending unless I deliberately took my hands away.

lines.japanese: いよいよ首や肩や目や心が疲れてきて、僕はハイスコアを更新しつづけるゲームを投げだし、立ちあがって伸びをした。
lines.english: At last my neck, shoulders, eyes, and heart all began to tire. I abandoned the game with its high score still climbing, rose, and stretched.

lines.japanese: いくらなんでも……遅いな、高内さん……。
lines.english: No matter how I looked at it… Takauchi was late. Very late…

lines.japanese: もしかして、という黒い予感が頭をよぎった。
lines.english: A dark possibility crossed my mind.

lines.japanese: もしかして、何か、ここに来られない災難にでも見まわれたんだろうか。
lines.english: Could some misfortune have kept her from coming?

lines.japanese: 学年主任に捕まって校則違反の化粧を咎められた、とかならまだいい。まさかもっと重大な怪我や急病で運ばれたとか──
lines.english: If the head of our year had caught her and reprimanded her for violating the rules against makeup, that would be fine. But what if she had been rushed away with a serious injury or sudden illness—

lines.japanese: ──僕は早足で窓辺へ寄って、救急車やストレッチャーでも来ていないものかと見下ろした。
lines.english: —I hurried to the window and looked down for an ambulance, or perhaps a stretcher.

lines.japanese: よかった、来てない。
lines.english: Good. There was none.

lines.japanese: それならいいや。
lines.english: Then everything was fine.

lines.japanese: 誰かが不幸になってないならそれでいい。僕ひとりが裏切られたり、時間を無駄にする程度のことはどうだっていい。いまさら渡来さんと並んで歩く夢が叶うわけでもないのだし。
lines.english: As long as no one had come to harm, that was enough. It hardly mattered if I alone was betrayed or had my time wasted. It was too late now for my dream of walking beside Watarai to come true.

lines.japanese: こんな風に訪れない相手を待ちつづける退屈な時間なら、これまでだって何度か過ごしたことがある。
lines.english: I had spent tedious hours like this before, waiting for someone who would never come.

lines.japanese: そんなのは、べつにどうだっていいんだ。
lines.english: It did not matter. Not in the least.

lines.japanese: そんなのは、世の中のいろいろに比べれば瑣末ごとだ。
lines.english: Compared with all the things in the world, it was trivial.

lines.japanese: 僕は１２月の無表情な空と街を眺めた。
lines.english: I gazed upon the expressionless city and sky of December.

lines.japanese: 何故だかふと豆パン君のことを思いだす。
lines.english: For some reason, I suddenly remembered Mamepan.

lines.japanese: 豆パン君はとある個人サイトの主催者で、僕はそこに設置された掲示板へ集う参加者のひとりだった。アニメやゲームの二次創作小説と、週に２～３回更新される日記がメインの小さなホームページだった。
lines.english: Mamepan ran a personal website, and I was one of the people who gathered on its message board. It was a small site devoted mainly to fanfiction about anime and games, along with a diary updated two or three times a week.

lines.japanese: 彼は僕と同い年だったみたいだけど、年齢のわりに文章がとても達者だった。将来は物書きになれればなあと、含羞を表す顔文字付きで語っていたこともあった。
lines.english: He seemed to be my age, but his writing was remarkably accomplished. Once, with a bashful emoticon, he confessed that he hoped to become a writer someday.

lines.japanese: 面白くて知識が豊富で人当たりも良かったけど、なにより、彼はとても強いひとだった。
lines.english: He was amusing, knowledgeable, and kind to everyone. More than anything, he was strong.

lines.japanese: 彼はしばしば日記において、愉快じゃない出来事をおどけた筆致で愉快に綴っていた。
lines.english: In his diary, he often transformed unpleasant events into entertaining stories through the comedy of his prose.

lines.japanese: 男性器をもじった仇名で呼ばれていること。足をひっかけて転ばされたこと。通学用の自転車を勝手に乗って行かれたこと。ノートや教科書に心ない落書きをされたこと。真冬のプールに突きおとされたこと。
lines.english: Being called by a nickname that mocked his genitals. Being tripped. Having his bicycle taken without permission. Finding cruel graffiti in his notebooks and textbooks. Being pushed into the swimming pool in the dead of winter.

lines.japanese: ＣＤやＤＶＤの万引きを手伝わされたこと。もらったばかりの小遣いを財布ごと持っていかれたこと。服をぜんぶ脱がされてケータイのカメラで撮られたこと。居並ぶ後輩たちの前で自慰行為を強要されたこと。
lines.english: Being forced to help shoplift CDs and DVDs. Having a newly received allowance stolen, wallet and all. Being stripped naked and photographed with a cell-phone camera. Being forced to masturbate in front of a line of younger students.

lines.japanese: 殴られたこと。蹴られたこと。叩かれたこと。絞められたこと。引きずりまわされたこと。
lines.english: Being punched. Kicked. Struck. Strangled. Dragged around.

lines.japanese: ある日、底の浅い正義感に燃える誰かが、プロバイダーを通して所轄の少年課に通報した。
lines.english: One day, someone ablaze with shallow righteousness contacted the local juvenile division through the site’s internet provider.

lines.japanese: それからしばらく更新が途絶えた。掲示板のみんなは、新作アニメの作画のひどさを嘆きながら彼の身の上を案じた。
lines.english: For a while, the updates stopped. The people on the message board lamented the dreadful animation in the latest anime while worrying about what had become of him.

lines.japanese: 一週間ほどして、豆パン君は何事もなかったようにひょっこり帰ってきた。
lines.english: About a week later, Mamepan popped back up as though nothing had happened.

lines.japanese: それ以来、日記の方向性ががらりと変わった。身を削ったブラックユーモアはどこかへ失せ、流行りのアニメやゲームの面白レビューが中心になった。
lines.english: From then on, his diary changed completely. The self-lacerating black humor disappeared. Amusing reviews of popular anime and games became its heart.

lines.japanese: 間が開いてしまったせいか、芸風が変わったせいか、訪問者は少しずつ減っていった。でも僕は文字にこそしなかったものの、そのさりげないリニューアルを心から祝福していた。
lines.english: Perhaps because of the interruption, or because his style had changed, visitors dwindled away little by little. I never put it into words, but in my heart I celebrated that quiet renewal.

lines.japanese: それからは連日更新が続いた。彼は愛する作品の長文感想を次々にアップした。対象作品は新しいものから古いものへと、まるで彼自身の人生を追憶するみたいにどんどん遡っていった。
lines.english: Then came updates every day. One after another, he posted long reflections upon the works he loved. Their subjects moved backward from the new to the old, as though he were retracing the course of his own life.

lines.japanese: どれも人柄の滲みでている優しい長文だった。彼は創作物に対しても同級生に対しても、自分以外を決して悪く言わないひとだった。そういうときは、それを受けいれられない自分の狭量さを責めるようなひとだった。
lines.english: Every post was long and gentle, steeped in his character. Whether speaking of fiction or his classmates, he never spoke ill of anyone but himself. When he could not accept something, he was the kind of person who blamed the narrowness of his own heart.

lines.japanese: すげえオナニーくさいんですが、と前置きして、オリジナルのファンタジー小説用プロットも公開した。どこかで見たような設定の焼き直しぽかったけど、膨大な熱意と労力が詰まっていることは感じとれた。
lines.english: With a warning that this was going to sound masturbatory as hell, he also unveiled an outline for an original fantasy novel. Its world seemed pieced together from settings I had seen before, yet I could feel the enormous devotion and labor packed inside it.

lines.japanese: その秘密のプロットを公開した日、彼は残り少なくなっていた掲示板の常連たちに一言ずつの全レスを付けた。僕へのメッセージはこうだった。
lines.english: The day he revealed that secret outline, he answered each of the few remaining regulars on the message board with a personal line. His message to me read:

lines.japanese: 『オマエの愛の深さに免じて穂乃香だけは譲ろう。だがその代わり翼ちんはオレが頂いた。いやっほう、自由の翼で豆パンＩ　ｃａｎ　ｆｌｙ！』
lines.english: ‘In deference to the fathomless depths of your love, I relinquish Honoka to you. In exchange, however, little Tsubasa is mine. Yee-haw! On wings of freedom, Mamepan—I can fly!’

lines.japanese: 藤宮穂乃香と小鳥遊翼は、どちらもささやきマテリアルの人気ヒロイン。僕と豆パン君は、よく穂乃香というキャラクターの魅力について深く語りあっていたんだ。
lines.english: Honoka Fujimiya and Tsubasa Takanashi were both popular heroines from *Whisper Material*. Mamepan and I often spoke at length about the charms of Honoka as a character.

lines.japanese: すぐに僕は冗談まじりのお礼と、そして、飛べると叫んだ彼への祝辞を書きこんだ。
lines.english: I immediately replied with joking thanks, followed by my congratulations to the man who had proclaimed that he could fly.

lines.japanese: 『ちょ、おまｗｗｗｗちょっとマテリアルｗｗｗｗｗ翼は俺の嫁フヒヒ、サーセンｗｗｗｗｗｗでも無問題ｗｗｗｗ人間はひとりでも飛べる（ソースは俺ｗｗっうぇｗｗｗっうぇｗｗｗｗｗ』
lines.english: ‘dude WHAT lmaoooo wait a Material lmaoooo Tsubasa is MINE lol, sry lmaoooo but no biggie lmaoooo a man can fly solo (source: me) LMAOOOO’

lines.japanese: しかし、そのレスに対するレスが付くことはなかった。
lines.english: But no answer ever came to that reply.

lines.japanese: 次の日の夕食どき、羽田の家でニュース番組を観ていた僕は、たまたま６０秒足らずにまとめられた小さな事件をひとつ知った。
lines.english: The following evening, as I watched the news over dinner at the Haneda house, I happened to learn of a minor incident compressed into less than sixty seconds.

lines.japanese: 春まで雪が降る海の向こうの地方都市で、細長い中層マンションの８階から飛びおりた少年。
lines.english: In a provincial city across the sea, where snow fell until spring, a boy had jumped from the eighth floor of a narrow mid-rise apartment building.

lines.japanese: その日を最後に、豆パン君のサイトは更新を断った。誰が呼びかけても返事をよこすことはなくなった。沈黙のまま時が過ぎ、ひとは去り、やがてアクセス不可になった。
lines.english: After that day, Mamepan’s site was never updated again. No matter who called out to him, no answer came. Time passed in silence. People left. Eventually the site could no longer be reached.

lines.japanese: 調べることは出来たかもしれない。だけど僕は、あえて豆パン君と飛びおりた少年の関連性を調べようとはしなかった。
lines.english: Perhaps I could have investigated. But I deliberately chose not to search for a connection between Mamepan and the boy who had jumped.

lines.japanese: だって僕は信じている。きっと彼は、春には雪が降らないどこかの街で、日記の更新さえ忘れるほどに夢中で、あの壮大な冒険活劇の完成を目指しているんだ。
lines.english: Because I believed. Surely, somewhere in a city where snow did not fall in spring, he was so absorbed in bringing that vast adventure to completion that he had forgotten even to update his diary.

lines.japanese: 僕のグレタガルドにも劣らない、あの夢とロマンの一大スペクタクルを。
lines.english: That grand spectacle of dreams and romance, no lesser than my own Gretagard.
